audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Levels 2-3 and first item to Cho'Gath and left 4-5 and 6 neutral, while the page's own whys give Aurora everything from Level 2 to first item. The lane is also graded TRICKY 7.5/10 despite a 53.45% win rate and an Aurora-sided chart.
audit.why: whys[1] to whys[5] read "chipping his HP before Feast stacks pad it", "out-trade an immobile Cho'Gath", "your poke, passive healing, and W cooldown all peak here", "burst and grab the W reset", "force all-ins... before his Feast HP scales out of reach". Only whys[6] gives the lane away, which is correct — Feast HP plus tank items ends the poke plan. 53.45% over 58 games backs a modest Aurora edge, not a tricky lane.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Aurora / Cho'Gath, and the grade moved from TRICKY 7.5/10 to FAV 5/10 with the matching tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named Aurora's ultimate "Between the Worlds" — no such ability — and gave no cooldown for either ultimate. Feast's timing is the whole reason the late stage flips.
audit.why: Feast is 80/70/60 seconds at 175 range and deals a high amount of true damage; Between Worlds is 140/120/100. So Cho'Gath can spend his ultimate roughly twice for every one of Aurora's, and each successful Feast permanently grows his health bar. That compounding, not a single burst, is what closes the poke window.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (140s) zones his all-in, and Feast is 80s of true damage — MR does nothing to it, so never sit low near him.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream is called "the silence" once in a Common Mistakes bullet and never explained; the page never says what a silence actually does to Aurora. Rupture's range is never given, and the page assumes Aurora out-ranges him.
audit.why: Feral Scream (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, 300 range cone) silences. Aurora's only two escapes, Across the Veil (22/21/20/19/18) and Between Worlds (140/120/100), are both casts — a silence takes both away at once, which is why his 300-range cone, not his knockup, is the thing that kills her. Rupture (Q) is 950 range on a flat 6-second cooldown, longer than Twofold Hex's 900, so he can trade poke with her from outside her own range and the delayed knockup interrupts anything she is casting. Vorpal Spikes (E, 8/7/6/5/4) adds a slow to every auto in a cone in front of him.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream silences for seconds at 300 range — silenced, you cannot cast Across the Veil.

audit.whatIsWrong: The only tracked cooldown on the page is Feast, with no number attached, and Rupture's 6-second cooldown is never mentioned.
audit.why: Feast is 80s at rank 1 and Rupture is 6s. Tracking Feast tells you when you can stand at low health; Rupture at 6s is effectively always up, so the advice "trade around his cooldown" is only meaningful for Feral Scream (11s) and Feast.
audit.corrected: Feast is 80s and true damage — MR will not save you, so never sit low.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].t reads "Build MR for his R". Feast is true damage; magic resist does nothing against it.
audit.why: Riot's kit file flags Feast trueDamage and percentHealth, and _missing/aurora.json flags Cho'Gath as a champion who bypasses stacking resistances via Feast. MR is still right against Rupture and Feral Scream, so the item advice survives — the reason attached to it does not.
audit.corrected: Build MR for his Q-W, not for Feast — Feast is true damage and ignores resistances entirely.
